title: Embedded Offline Packaging and Licensing Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the product-level requirements, packaging options, licensing flows, and rollout roadmap for 'Embedded Offline' — a variant of Redwood’s inference runtime packaged for customer-hosted, intermittent-network, and air-gapped environments. It covers the commercial SKUs, technical constraints, on-device telemetry 'quiet mode', offline upgrade flow, and the release criteria for an initial 1.0 launch.

Why this exists

- Customers in regulated industries and edge deployments require deterministic, auditable on-device inference that operates when connectivity is unavailable or restricted.
- We need a repeatable packaging model that balances unit economics, security, and a predictable upgrade/telemetry story for product and revenue teams.

Goals (high level)

1. Define three commercial SKUs (Developer, Edge, Enterprise) with clear entitlements and limits.
2. Ship an offline upgrade and license activation flow that does not require outbound networking (using signed license manifests).
3. Provide a telemetry "quiet mode" that aggregates minimal telemetry and supports batched uploading when connectivity returns.
4. Achieve parity of inference contract (API surface) with hosted Redwood API, enabling a smooth hosted-to-embedded migration path.
5. Meet baseline security and compliance controls: KMS integration option, signed binaries, and an audit log export utility.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: packaging artifacts, licensing model, UX for license activation, offline upgrade mechanics, telemetry policy, pricing guidance for SKUs, and release criteria.
- Out of scope: creation of new base models or model training; integrations with third-party secure enclaves (beyond KMS/HSM reference).

Requirements (functional)

ID | Requirement | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria
R-001 | Offline license activation via signed manifest (no outbound call) | P0 | product | License manifest applied by local CLI or UI; runtime refuses to start without valid signed manifest; manifest expiry enforced.
R-002 | Telemetry quiet mode with batched upload | P0 | eng-platform | Telemetry file created locally (max 50MB/day) and encrypted; uploaded when customer toggles sync or connectivity resumes.
R-003 | SKU enforcement: token/throughput caps per license | P1 | finance-legal | Runtime enforces soft limits (throttling) and records overage events to audit log.
R-004 | API surface parity with hosted text-generation endpoints (subset: generate/chat/embeddings) | P1 | eng-serving-runtime | Example app can switch from hosted API to local endpoint with no code changes aside from base URL.
R-005 | Signed binary verification at startup | P0 | security | Startup fails if binary signature mismatch; verification logs written to audit export.
R-006 | Offline patch/upgrade using signed bundle | P1 | eng-infra | Admin can apply an upgrade bundle file; rollback supported if health checks fail within 5 minutes.

Technical design (overview)

- Components:
  - embedded-runtime: stripped container/binary hosting inference runtime and a small management agent (redwood-embedded-agent).
  - license-agent: local CLI/UI to apply signed license manifests and manage grace periods.
  - telemetry-aggregator: local process that writes encrypted batches to disk and exposes an opt-in sync command.
  - upgrade-applier: verifies signed bundles, runs preflight checks, and performs atomic swap with rollback.

- Security model:
  - All manifests and bundles are RSA-4096 signed by Redwood. Customers may integrate their KMS to re-sign internal manifests for private variants.
  - Audit log format: newline-delimited JSON entries, encrypted with AES-256 and exportable via CLI.

Example license manifest (YAML)

---
license_id: "EMB-ENT-001"
issued_to: "example-customer"
sku: "enterprise"
throughput_tokens_per_min: 20000
valid_from: "2026-06-01"
valid_until: "2027-05-31"
signature: "<base64-sig>"
---

Offline upgrade commands (examples)

# Verify bundle signature (local)
$ redwood-embedded-agent verify-bundle ./bundle-v1.1.tar.sig

# Apply signed bundle
$ sudo redwood-embedded-agent apply-bundle ./bundle-v1.1.tar.sig --atomic 

Telemetry behavior

- Default mode: telemetry minimal (health, startup/shutdown, license events). No request-level tokens or prompt content.
- Quiet mode: default for all Embedded SKUs. Operators can enable full telemetry for troubleshoot windows for up to 72 hours; full telemetry requires explicit local admin consent and an expiration timestamp.
- Telemetry retention on device: 14 days by default or configurable by policy file.

Packaging and SKUs (commercial guidance)

- Developer (Free/Trial): single-node, 1M tokens/day cap, 30-day license, includes local dev tooling and developer console.
- Edge: multi-instance on single site, 10M tokens/day cap, 12-month license, basic support, telemetry quiet mode default.
- Enterprise: unlimited site licensing with defined throughput bands (customer selects band), annual support & security assessment, KMS/HSM integration, commercial SLA.

Pricing guidance (illustrative)

- Developer: free to $199/month (trial conversions)
- Edge: $1,500/month + volume token surcharge over cap
- Enterprise: custom quote — baseline $25k/year for smallest band; add-on for KMS/HSM and air-gap packaging.

Roadmap & rollout phases

Phase 0 (MVP, Q3 2026):
- Deliver offline license manifest flow, signed binary verification, telemetry quiet-mode, and Developer/Edge SKU definitions.
- Pilot with two existing mid-market customers in regulated verticals.

Phase 1 (stability & packaging, Q4 2026):
- Add enterprise SKU entitlements, upgrade applier with rollback, audit export tooling, and automated health-check pain points.

Phase 2 (commercialization, Q1 2027):
- Pricing finalization, packaging for on-prem partners, marketplace listing, and legal/compliance sign-offs.

Release criteria (1.0):
- All P0 requirements implemented and verified by QA.
- Successful pilot with at least one customer running a production workload for 14 days without manual vendor intervention.
- Security review completed and signed off by Security & Compliance.

SLOs and metrics to watch

- Upgrade success rate >= 99% (per bundle application)
- License validation failure rate < 0.1% (false negatives)
- Telemetry upload success (when enabled) >= 95% within 24 hours of connectivity return
- Mean time to recovery (MTR) for rollback flows < 5 minutes

Operational runbook (high level)

1. License activation fails:
   a. Check signature verification logs: /var/log/redwood/license-verify.log
   b. Validate manifest timestamp and clock skew on device (NTP).
   c. If offline activation needed, request reissued manifest via Account Manager with customer-supplied public key.
2. Upgrade fails post-apply:
   a. Trigger automated rollback (applier will run if health-checks fail).
   b. Collect audit export and escalate to eng-platform with runbook id EMB-UPG-001.

Documentation & support materials

- User guide: embedded-offline-admin-guide.md (covering CLI and UI flows).
- Quickstart: one-click dev image + local sample app to mimic hosted API.
- Support playbook: embedded-incident-playbook.md referencing oncall paging and escalation matrix.

Open decisions

- D-01: Should we offer on-device per-route metering or only token-level caps? (impact: billing complexity)
- D-02: Accept third-party re-signing of bundles for OEM partners or require Redwood-managed key escrow?

Owners & contacts

Next steps

- Complete engineering spike for the offline bundle verification flow (owner: Anton) by 2026-06-30.
- Legal to draft license manifest T&C template (owner: Rafael) by 2026-07-10.
- Pilot onboarding checklist and pilot recruitment (owner: Customer Success) by 2026-07-15.
